title: PowerPoint: Copilot for creating and editing presentations in GCC
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, add-on licensing and licence-assignment controls are supported. It correctly reports the service description's different GCC editing availability and leaves the release default and government-cloud brand-kit availability unconfirmed.

claims.claim: The brand-kit governance page describes two independent policies.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot provides two independent policies for brand kit governance:

claims.claim: The Enterprise Brand Manager policy controls publication, editing and management of official brand kits.
claims.quote: Enterprise Brand Manager policy | Who can publish, edit, and manage official brand kits. | Members of the brand manager mail-enabled security group specified in the policy.

claims.claim: The Restrict brand kit creation policy controls creation and editing of personal brand kits.
claims.quote: Restrict brand kit creation policy | Who can create and edit personal brand kits. | Members of the mail-enabled security group specified in the policy.

claims.claim: The two named brand-kit policies govern brand-kit creation and publication, not Copilot in PowerPoint availability.
claims.quote: Brand kit policies control who can create personal brand kits and who can publish or manage official brand kits.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses is the documented route to product licence assignment.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence through Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()
